subject_line: The number that changes first (most people miss it)
opening: Hey, we've got a packed issue this week and one story that's already getting forwarded like crazy. If you've ever sat in a doctor's office and heard something that scared you, Sarah's piece is going to feel like a hand on your shoulder. Plus, we've got the real talk on keeping weight off once you've hit your goal, and yes, we're covering the vegetable thing. Let's get into it.

hero.title: Prediabetes After 55: What Carnivore Changes First
hero.teaser: You go in for a routine checkup, and the doctor uses a word you weren't expecting. Prediabetes. Suddenly you're staring at a number on a printout and wondering what comes next. The thing is, not all the markers move at the same speed, and knowing which one tends to shift first can change how you read your own progress. Sarah breaks down the sequence, so you're not guessing while you wait for your next labs.

supporting.title: Hit Your Goal Weight? How to Eat So It Stays Off
supporting.teaser: Marcus lays out exactly why the eating plan that got you to goal is the wrong plan for staying there, and what to do instead.

supporting.title: Intermittent Fasting on Carnivore for Women Over 50
supporting.teaser: Sarah found a hidden cost that most fasting protocols don't warn women over 50 about, and it quietly shows up on the scale months later.

supporting.title: Missing Vegetables on Carnivore? What Readers Do
supporting.teaser: People who've been eating this way for years eventually figure out something about vegetable cravings that nobody tells beginners.

try_this_week: Pull out your most recent blood work and find your fasting glucose number. If you don't have one, call your doctor's office today and ask what's on file. Knowing your starting point is the whole game, and Sarah's piece on pre-carnivore blood tests will tell you exactly what else to ask for before you change anything.
looking_ahead: Next week we're getting into something community members keep asking about quietly: what happens to your sleep when you go carnivore, and whether the first few weeks are supposed to feel this weird.
